purpose: Machine-readable repository architecture contract for top-level ownership and lifecycle boundaries.

.github.note: GitHub-native automation boundary; remains at repository root by platform contract.

apps.note: Canonical container for maintained application source whose deployed URL layout is staged independently; contains the current Rules Arbiter browser shell and embedded Rules Arbiter widget presentation source, plus Card Reference, Deckbuilder, Factions, Rules, Start, Playtest, About, Accessibility, Changelog, Contact, FAQ, Press, and Privacy surfaces.

artifacts.note: Build/reconstruction/QA evidence pending retention audit; Rules Arbiter historical/manual QA audit reports live under artifacts/rules-qa/audits/.

card-design.note: Maintained canonical browser face rendering, authority-linked component presentation, and canonical family styles. Environment-neutral face authority lives under packages/rendering/; artwork authoring/compositor source lives under tools/card-design/artwork-authoring/; review/catalog/inspection/direct-card preparation source lives under tools/card-design/review/; compatibility-only render/review entrypoints live under legacy/public-compatibility/card-design/; historical studies live under legacy/. Stable /card-design/ URLs remain materialized independently of repository placement.

config.note: Maintained cross-system configuration; root placement is deliberate.

docs.note: Maintained documentation and explicitly archived development records, including current card-design standards under docs/card-design/.

governance.note: Decision provenance, schemas, traceability, and audit records.

images.note: Source and derived visual assets remain mixed pending asset-lifecycle audit.

legacy.note: Explicitly non-authoritative historical implementation/publication/source provenance. The Browser Rulebook shell remains under legacy/rulebook-browser/ as a transitional deployment source for /rulebook/; compatibility-only card-design entrypoints live under legacy/public-compatibility/card-design/; historical Rules Arbiter compatibility source lives under legacy/rules-assistant/, including withdrawn/candidate v062 plus still-routed v063, v070, and v071 implementations.

media.note: Current reproducible media/composition configuration and export tooling.

packages.note: Canonical container for maintained shared packages and authorities; contains the complete current game-data authority, maintained active rules source/publication support, current rule-fact synchronization helper, and shared rendering model authority under packages/rendering/.

rulebook.note: Legacy monolithic Rulebook source, version-specific compatibility support, and Rulebook QR assets. Gameplay authority lives at packages/game-data/current-game.json; maintained rules support lives under packages/rules/; current /rulebook/ content is the modular v0.7.2 publication rather than this legacy root.

rules-assistant.note: Transitional Rules Arbiter backend/shared-runtime root: current Worker routing and retrieval, D1 migrations, runtime-adjacent regression tests, and remaining explicitly versioned compatibility helpers. Historical v062, v063, v070, and v071 Worker/corpus implementations now live under legacy/rules-assistant/ while the current Worker entry preserves their explicit routes. Browser presentation, admin/refinement/QA tooling, and retained QA evidence live in their separated boundaries.

scripts.note: Cross-project generation, validation, release, migration, and maintenance tooling.

tests.note: Repository-wide contract/regression harness; root placement is deliberate.

tts.note: TTS generation/packaging plus versioned release evidence.

v0.7.1.note: Historical v0.7.1 versioned public entrypoint retained for release compatibility.

v0.7.2.note: Lifecycle-selected current v0.7.2 versioned public release entrypoint.

tools.note: Canonical container for maintained production tooling whose source placement is independent from public routes; contains card-design authoring/review tooling and Rules Arbiter admin, refinement, and QA/evaluation tooling under tools/rules-assistant/.
